JNJ.rationale: JNJ is a high-quality franchise executing a portfolio transition, but the quantitative evidence is unambiguously negative at current levels. PE at 26.8x sits at the 99th percentile of its 365-day range while ROE has declined from 31.7% to 25.9% — the market is paying peak multiples for deteriorating returns. Gross margins compressed from 69.6% to 66.3% QoQ, Q4 operating cash flow collapsed 72.6% to $2.51B, and the earnings yield of 3.7% is below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.45%, eliminating the defensive-valuation rationale. The Q1 2025 one-time gain inflates TTM metrics. While Q1 2026 results showed 9.9% revenue growth and FY2026 guidance of $100.3B–$101.3B revenue / $11.45–$11.65 adjusted EPS is solid, the stock is already priced for perfection. A reversion to the median PE of ~20x implies ~25% downside. The Stelara biosimilar cliff will deepen through 2026–2027, talc litigation remains unresolved, and rising rates make the 3.7% earnings yield uncompetitive. No near-term catalyst justifies the premium; the risk/reward is asymmetrically to the downside.
